body:
다음 <보기>의 영영풀이가 알맞지 않은 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
ⓐ gate: the structure that covers or forms the
top of a building, vehicle, tent etc
ⓑ award: a prize or money that is given to
someone following an official decision
ⓒ clean: to remove dirt from something by
rubbing or washing
ⓓ leave: to come or go back from one place to
another
ⓔ present: to give something to somebody, especially
formally at a ceremony
solution: ⓐ gate는 ‘문, 정문’이라는 뜻으로, 주어진 영영풀이인 ‘건물, 탈 것, 텐트 등의 꼭대기를 덮거나 형성하는 구조물’은 roof(지 붕)의 영영풀이이므로 알맞지 않다. ‘the part of a fence or wall that you can open and close to enter or leave a place(장소에 들어가거나 나가기 위해 당신이 열고 닫을 수 있 는 울타리나 벽의 일부분)’로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ leave는 ‘떠나다’라는 뜻으로, 주어진 영영풀이인 ‘한 장소에 서 다른 장소로 오거나 돌아가다’는 return의 영영풀이이므로 알맞지 않다. ‘to go away from a place or a person(한 장소 나 사람으로부터 떠나다)’로 고쳐야 한다.

다음 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?

B: Look! Here is a poster for the talent show.
G: Cool! I heard that Jia will sing a song at the show.
B: Yeah, I’m looking forward to watching her
performance.
G: She sings very well. ________________________________
B: I think she will!
ⓐ It’s possible that she will win first prize!
ⓑ I doubt that she will win first prize.
ⓒ I’m unsure if she will win first prize.
ⓓ Maybe she will win first prize!
ⓔ I think she will win first prize!
solution: 지아가 장기자랑 대회에서 노래할 것이라고 들었다는 소녀의 말에 소년이 그녀의 공연이 기대된다고 했으며 소녀는 지아가 노래 를 정말 잘한다고 말하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 긍정적인 가능성 이나 기대가 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 지아의 1등 가 능성을 언급하는 ⓐ, ⓓ, ⓔ가 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절하다. NE능률(김기택) 3과

running my booth.

need to bring some old clothes.
B: That’s a great idea. Do you need any help? I can
give you a hand.

work with me.
B: I’ll do it. And maybe Mingyu will join us, too.
G: That sounds perfect. I’ll ask him!

B: I’m looking forward to playing some games today.
G: Me too. This balloon game looks fun. Why don’t
we try it?
B: Wait, maybe Taemin will want to join us.
G: You’re right. He likes all kinds of games. I’ll call
him and ask him.
B: All right.

What kind of game does the girl suggest trying?
Why do the girl and boy think Taemin mightwant to join the game?
What game does Taemin like the most?
What will the girl do after the dialogue?
solution: 태민이가 모든 종류의 게임을 좋아한다는 내용은 있으나 가장 좋아하는 게임이 무엇인지에 대한 언급은 없으므로 ❹ ‘태민이 는 어떤 게임을 가장 좋아하는가?’는 답할 수 없는 질문이다.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

solution: (A) 문장의 동사로 started가 있으므로, 접속사 없이 다른 과거 동사 looked는 올 수 없고, started의 목적어가 와야 하며, 동사 start는 목적어로 to부정사와 동명사를 모두 취할 수 있으므로 과거동사 started의 목적어로 to부정사 to look이 적절하다. (B) 동사 agree는 목적어로 ‘접속사 that+주어+동사 ~’ 형태의 명사절을 취할 수 있으므로, 주어와 동사를 갖춘 완전한 절 (the roads needed more lights)을 이끌어, 과거동사 agreed의 목적어인 명사절을 이루는 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다. (C) 형용사를 취해 ‘~하게 느끼다, ~한 느낌이 나다’라는 뜻으 로 쓰이는 감각 동사 feel의 보어 자리로, 형용사 safe는 1음절 이고 –e로 끝나므로 –r을 붙여 만든 비교급 safer가 적절하다.

solution: 두 번째 문장의 주어인 It이 첫 번째 문장의 the new shop을 가리키고 있으므로 두 문장을 서로 이어주는 접속사와 주어 역할의 대명사라는 두 가지 역할을 동시에 하는 주격 관계대 명사를 이용하여 연결한 형태인 I like the new shop+관계사 절(주격 관계대명사+동사 ~)의 형태가 되어야 한다. 선행사인 the new shop은 사물이므로 관계대명사 that 또는 which가 와야 하고, 주격 관계대명사 뒤에 이어지는 동사는 선행사에 수일치 해야 하므로 단수명사구인 선행사에 수일치한 단수동 사 sells가 쓰여야 한다. 따라서 두 문장을 연결한 것으로 ❹‘I like the new shop that sells strange things.(나는 이상한 물 건들을 파는 그 새로운 가게를 좋아해.)‘가 적절하다.

body:
Siyeon
I try to cheer up my friends when they are having
a hard time. One day, Jisu posted, “(A)[That / It]
was a hard day,” on her social media. I wanted to
do something to make her (B)[happy / happily]. So,
I bought her chocolate cookies, her favorite snack.
Then we watched a movie that had a funny story
and (C)[taking / took] pictures together at a photo
booth. We had a great time, and she said she felt
better.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 지칭하는 대상이 없으며, a hard day(힘든 하루)라는 상황 을 나타내는 말이 이어지고 있으므로 의미 없이 주어 자리에 쓰이는 비인칭주어 It이 적절하다. (B) make의 목적어 her에 이어진 목적격보어 자리로, ’make+ 목적어+목적격보어(형용사)‘가 ’~를 …하게 만들다‘라는 뜻을 나타내므로, 형용사 happy가 적절하다. (C) 주어 we가 영화를 보고 사진을 찍은 것이므로, we의 과거 동사 watched와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬 연결된 동사 자 리임을 알 수 있다. 따라서 과거동사 took가 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 우리말 뜻이 어색한 것은?

Another interesting question ⓐwas asked by morning412.
morning412: How much sleep do we need?
In a study, researchers found that teenagers need 8 to 10 hours of sleep each night. However, ⓑthe quality of sleep matters, too.
Here is a simple tip for having a deep sleep: ⓒPut your phone down 30 minutes to an hour before you go to bed. Looking at videos or messages ⓓkeeps your brain active. So, if you bring your phone to bed, you ⓔmay have trouble falling asleep.
Did you enjoy today’s live stream? Sleep well, and see you next time!
choices: ⓔ: 잠드는 데 어려움을 겪을 수 있습니다
solution:
1. ⓓ keeps your brain active는 'keep+목적어+형용사(~을 …한 상태로 유지하다)' 구조이다.
2. 따라서 '여러분의 뇌를 활동적인 상태로 유지합니다'가 알맞고, '뇌가 활동하는 것을 막습니다'는 정반대의 뜻이다.
3. ⓐ 수동태(~에 의해 질문되었다), ⓑ matter(중요하다), ⓒ put down(내려놓다), ⓔ have trouble -ing(~하는 데 어려움을 겪다)는 모두 알맞다.
따라서 답은 ④이다.

(C) So(그래서)로 연결된 결과의 문장에서 만약 침대에 휴대전 화를 가지고 간다면, 잠드는 데 어려움을 겪을 수 있다고 했으 므로, 동영상이나 메시지를 보는 것이 뇌를 ‘활발하게’ 한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 active가 적절하다.

body:
Sleep is so important that you can’t live without it.
When you sleep, your body repairs your cells and
muscles. So, if you don’t get enough sleep, you can
get sick.
Sleep is important for your physical health. And it
is also important for your memory. (A)여러분이 잠을
자는 동안, 여러분의 뇌는 필요 없는 기억들을 정리합
니다. This makes space for new memories. Imagine
keeping every detail of your experiences in your
memory. It would be like a room with unnecessary
items everywhere.
sweetdream: During sleep, the brain works like a
cleaner.
Sweetdream made a good point. Yes, unnecessary
memories are cleaned up by your brain while you
sleep.
Now, let’s look at some questions. Here’s an
interesting one.
sleepy: I have so much homework on weekdays
that I can’t sleep enough. So, I sleep more
on weekends. Is this okay?
Trying to sleep a lot during weekends may help.
But you should try to keep a regular sleep
schedule. Changing sleep patterns too often may
lead to health problems.
Another interesting question was asked by morning412.
morning412: How much sleep do we need?
In a study, researchers found that teenagers need
8 to 10 hours of sleep each night. However, the
quality of sleep matters, too.
Here is a simple tip for having a deep sleep: Put
your phone down 30 minutes to an hour before
you go to bed. Looking at videos or messages
keeps your brain active. So, if you bring your
phone to bed, (B)______________________________________.

윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: you may have trouble falling asleep
you will fall asleep as soon as you lie down
blue light from your phone will hurt your eyes
solution: 정답은 ③ 이다. (해설 없음)

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 어색한 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
ⓐ enough: to the degree that is necessary or wanted
ⓑ clear: to remove things that are not wanted or
needed from something
ⓒ imagine: to have a particular opinion or to
believe that something is true
ⓓ regular: not happening or done at the normal
time for doing something
ⓔ active: staying still and calm without any movement
solution: ⓒ imagine은 ‘상상하다’라는 뜻이므로, 주어진 영영풀이인 ‘특 정한 의견을 가지거나 어떤 것이 사실이라고 믿다’는 think(생 각하다)의 풀이이므로 적절하지 않다. ‘to make an idea or picture of something in your mind(어떤 것의 아이디어나 그 림을 당신의 마음에 만들어보다)’로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ regular는 ‘규칙적인’이라는 뜻이므로, 주어진 영영풀이인 ‘어떤 일을 해야 하는 보통의 시간에 일어나지 않거나 이루어 지지 않는’은 irregular(불규칙한)의 풀이이므로 적절하지 않다. ‘happening or doing something often, especially at the same time every week, year, etc.(특히 매주, 매년 등 같은 시간에 자주 일어나거나 어떤 것을 하는)’로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ active는 ‘활발한’이라는 뜻이므로, 주어진 영영풀이인 ‘어떤 움직임 없이 가만히 그리고 차분하게 유지하는’은 적절하지 않다. ‘always busy doing things, especially physical or mental activities(무언가, 특히 신 체적이거나 정신적인 활동을 하느라 항상 바쁜)’으로 고쳐야 한다.

Warm Hearts, a club at our school. Our club has
solved some problems in our school and our
community over the past few years. I want to share
our stories.
One day, our school principal announced, “Our
students often take too much food and waste it at
lunchtime. How can we reduce food waste?”
The members of Warm Hearts gathered to solve
this problem. We thought that adding lines to food
trays would be helpful. Students could look at the

than before!

may think it’s easy. But some people have trouble
using kiosks.
To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at
the community center. We explained every step of
ordering: starting an order, choosing from the
menu, and paying.
After the class, people said, “Now we feel more
comfortable with kiosks. Thank you so much!” We
felt very proud.
As you can see, your actions can make positive
changes. Even the smallest acts can make a big
difference!

Sleep is so important that you can’t live without it.
When you sleep, your body (A)[damages / repairs]
your cells and muscles. So, if you don’t get enough
sleep, you can get sick.
Sleep is important for your physical health. And it
is also important for your memory. While you sleep,
your brain clears memories that are not needed.
This makes space for new memories. Imagine
keeping every detail of your experiences in your
memory. It would be like a room with unnecessary
items everywhere.
sweetdream: During sleep, the brain works like a
cleaner.
Sweetdream made a good point. Yes, unnecessary
memories are cleaned up by your brain while you
sleep.
Now, let’s look at some questions. Here’s an
interesting one.
sleepy: I have so much homework on weekdays
that I can’t sleep enough. So, I sleep more
on weekends. Is this okay?
Trying to sleep a lot during weekends may be
(B)[helpful / harmful]. But you should try to keep a
regular sleep schedule. Changing sleep patterns too
often may lead to health problems.
Another interesting question was asked by morning412.
morning412: How much sleep do we need?
In a study, researchers found that teenagers need
8 to 10 hours of sleep each night. However, the
quality of sleep matters, too.
Here is a simple tip for having a deep sleep: Put
your phone down 30 minutes to an hour before
you go to bed. Looking at videos or messages
keeps your brain (C)[active / relaxed]. So, if you
bring your phone to bed, you may have trouble
falling asleep.

Hello, everyone! I’m Yuna, and I’m the leader of
Warm Hearts, a club at our school. Our club has
solved some problems in our school and our
community over the past few years. I want to share
our stories.
One day, our school principal announced, “Our
students often take too much food and waste it at
lunchtime. How can we reduce food waste?”
The members of Warm Hearts gathered to solve
this problem. We thought that adding lines to food
trays would be helpful. Students could look at the
lines and take the right amount of food.
Our school principal liked this idea, so he changed
the food trays in the cafeteria. It was a success!
The new trays reduced a large amount of food
waste!
After we solved this problem at our school, we
started to look for problems in our community. We
found out that some roads around our school were
very dark at night. We all agreed that the roads
needed more lights. With the help of a teacher, we
put up lights with sensors around the
neighborhood. Now all our neighbors feel safer
than before!
Have you ever used a digital kiosk before? You
may think it’s easy. But some people have trouble
using kiosks.
To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at
the community center. We explained every step of
ordering: starting an order, choosing from the
menu, and paying.
After the class, people said, “Now we feel more
comfortable with kiosks. Thank you so much!” We
felt very proud.
As you can see, your actions can make positive
changes. Even the smallest acts can make a big
difference!

solution: (A) 명사 time을 수식해 ‘~할 시간이다’라는 뜻의 ‘it’s time+to 부정사‘ 구문을 이루는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사가 필요하므 로, 앞의 to와 함께 to부정사를 이루는 get up이 적절하다. (B) 날씨, 시간, 거리 등은 문장의 주어로 비인칭 주어 It을 사 용해 나타내므로, 날씨(sunny)를 나타내는 문장의 주어로 비인 칭 주어 It이 적절하다. (C) ’~ 동안‘이라는 전치사 for 뒤에는 ’얼마간의 기간‘을 나타내 는 명사(구)가 보통 숫자와 함께 쓰이나, 같은 뜻의 전치사 during 뒤에는 ’특정 기간, 특정 사건‘을 나타내는 명사(구)가 이 어져 그 특정 기간 안에 일어난 활동 등을 나타낸다. 따라서 특 정 기간의 명사구 lunch break 앞에 전치사 during이 적절하다.

solution: (A) 스위스는 집에서 햄스터나 앵무새를 한 마리만 키울 수 없 으며 최소 두 마리를 키워야 하는데, 반려동물들은 혼자 있을 때 ‘외롭게(lonely)’ 느낀다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. body:
Every country has its own culture. Culture shows
ways of living and thinking. In each culture, there
are rules that ⓐdoesn't allow certain things. So, we
need to know how ⓑacts in different countries.
Here are some unique and interesting rules from
around the world.
Switzerland: Let’s Care for Pets
In Switzerland, people really care about animals.
Swiss law says that people cannot have just one
hamster or one parrot at home. They must have at
least two. These pets feel lonely when they are
alone. They need a friend that can be with them.
Also, people who have dogs or cats must spend
enough time with their pets. Those who has dogs
must take them outside for exercise too. Pets are
very happy in Switzerland.
Singapore: Let’s ⓒKeeping the City Clean
Singapore is a very clean city. Here, people cannot
eat or drink on buses or the subway. They also
cannot sell or import chewing gum. Those actions
can make the city dirty and messy. People who
break the rules must pay a fine. In Singapore,
everyone knows where to eat and where to throw
away their trash. Thanks to these rules, Singapore
remains very clean.
France: Let French Children Love Their Food
In France, children can’t have ketchup in school
cafeterias. This sounds surprising, but there’s a good
reason. France is famous for its delicious food.
French people are very proud of their food. They
believe ⓓwhich ketchup hides the real taste of their
food. They really hope that their children can taste
and enjoy the flavors of French cooking. That way,
French children can learn to love their food culture.
Which rule is most surprising? Maybe some rules
sound ⓔstrangely to you, but they show different
lifestyles around the world. Understanding different
rules from different countries helps us live together
more happily.

ⓐ side: the form that something has, for example
round, square, triangular etc.
ⓑ lie: to be in a position in which your body is
flat on the floor, on a bed etc.

do or should do

to full length

solution: ⓐ side는 ‘옆, 측면’이라는 뜻으로, 주어진 영영풀이인 ‘예를 들어, 원형, 사각형, 삼각형과 같이 무언가가 가진 형태’는 shape(형태) 의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않다. ‘a position directly next to someone or something, on the right or the left(누군가 또는 무언가 바 로 옆, 오른쪽 또는 왼쪽에 있는 위치)'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ repeat은 ’반복하다‘라는 뜻으로, 주어진 영영풀이인 ’당신이 평소에 하거나 해야 하는 일을 하지 않다‘는 skip(건너뛰다, 생 략하다)의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않다. ’to say or do something again(무언가를 다시 말하거나 하다)‘으로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
Many students have “turtle neck.” This happens
when their head sticks forward. It often comes from
using smartphones, studying, or sitting for a long
time. When you have turtle neck, you may get neck
pain, back pain, or headaches. But don’t worry! Here
are some easy stretches to help with turtle neck.
Desk Stretch
Sit up straight and move your head slowly from
side to side. Put your right hand on the left side of
your head. Then gently pull your head to the right.
Hold for 5 seconds. Repeat on your left side.
Finally, put your hands together and hold your chin
with your thumbs. Push your head back slowly.
Hold for 10 seconds. If you do this set of stretches,
you’ll feel better.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(C)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 차례대로 연결된 것은?

(A) When you start desk stretching, you should
move your head quickly left and right.
(B) You should place your right hand on the opposite
side of your head during a desk stretch.
(C) When you do a desk stretch, you should hold
your chin with your thumbs after putting your
hands together.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(C)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 차례대로 연결된 것은?

다음 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 단어가 차례대로 연결된 것은?

up.
ⓐ hold  ⓑ lie  ⓒ bend  ⓓ spread
solution: (A) ⓑ lie  (B) ⓐ hold  (C) ⓓ spread  (D) ⓒ bend • 차가운 바닥에 (A)눕지 마. - lie(눕다) • 당신의 머리를 똑바로 (B)유지하세요. - hold(유지하다) • 균형을 유지하기 위해 당신의 다리를 (C)벌려라. - spread(벌 리다) • 그는 몸을 아래로 (D)굽혀 그것을 집기 위해 멈췄다. - bend (굽히다)

Desk Stretch
Sit up straight and ㉠move your head slowly from
side to side. Put your right hand on the left side of
your head. Then gently ㉡pull your head to the
right. Hold for 5 seconds. Repeat on your left side.
Finally, ㉢put your hands together and hold your
chin with your thumbs. Push your head back slowly.
Hold for 10 seconds. ⓐ여러분이 이 스트레칭 세트를
한다면 여러분은 더 나아짐을 느낄 것이다.
Standing Stretch
Stand and spread your feet. Bend your arms

much worse than she thought. It was dirty, messy,
and full of bugs! Nightingale knew that dirty
hospitals could be bad for the soldiers. More
soldiers got sick and died in the dirty hospital than
in battle. She wanted to change that. She asked
England to make the hospital much cleaner and
safer. However, the leaders of England didn’t
understand. To help them see the problem, she
collected data about the number of wounded and
dead soldiers. However, showing her findings with
just numbers was difficult.
To solve this problem, Nightingale created a
simple picture. It is called Nightingale’s rose
diagram. The diagram looked like a rose with
twelve petals. Each petal showed a month, and
larger petals meant more deaths. In the rose
diagram, (A)Nightingale에 의해 세 개의 다른 색깔들

disease, red is for battle wounds, and black is for
other causes. Surprisingly, the blue part was the
largest! Nightingale used this diagram (B)____________
___________________________________. She was very smart
and creative.

body:
Every country has its own culture. Culture shows
ways of living and thinking. In each culture, there
are rules that don’t allow certain things. So, we
need to know how to act in different countries.
Here are some unique and interesting rules from
around the world.
Switzerland: Let’s Care for Pets
In Switzerland, people really care about animals.
Swiss law says that people cannot have just one
hamster or one parrot at home. They must have at
least two. These pets feel lonely when they are
alone. They need a friend that can be with them.
Also, people who have dogs or cats must spend
enough time with their pets. Those who have dogs
must take them outside for exercise too. Pets are
very happy in Switzerland.
Singapore: Let’s Keep the City Clean
Singapore is a very clean city. Here, people cannot
eat or drink on buses or the subway. They also
cannot sell or import chewing gum. Those actions
can make the city dirty and messy. People who
break the rules must pay a fine. In Singapore,
everyone knows where to eat and where to throw
away their trash. Thanks to these rules, Singapore
remains very clean.
France: Let French Children Love Their Food
In France, children can’t have ketchup in school
cafeterias. This sounds surprising, but there’s a good
reason. France is famous for its delicious food.
French people are very proud of their food. They
believe that ketchup hides the real taste of their
food. They really hope that their children can taste
and enjoy the flavors of French cooking. That way,
French children can learn to love their food culture.
Which rule is most surprising? Maybe some rules
sound strange to you, but they show different
lifestyles around the world. Understanding different
rules from different countries helps us live together
more happily.

Many students have “turtle neck.” This happens
when their head sticks forward. It often comes from
using smartphones, studying, or sitting for a long
time. When you have turtle neck, you may get neck
pain, back pain, or headaches. But don’t worry!
Here are some easy stretches to help with turtle
neck.
Desk Stretch
Sit up straight and move your head slowly from
side to side. Put your right hand on the left side of
your head. Then gently pull your head to the right.
Hold for 5 seconds. Repeat on your left side.
Finally, put your hands together and hold your chin
with your thumbs. Push your head back slowly.
Hold for 10 seconds. (A)___________ you do this set
of stretches, you’ll feel better.
Standing Stretch
Stand and spread your feet. Bend your arms ⓐ(make)
a W shape. Then lean your head backward. Look up
at a 45-degree angle. Hold for 10 seconds. ㉠This
stretch is great for your neck and shoulders.
Bedtime Stretch
Lie on your bed with your head at the edge. ㉡당

seconds. Don’t do this for longer than 60 seconds.

ⓒ(relax) your neck and back.

________________. When you are sitting, ⓓ(sit) up
straight and keep your feet on the floor.

body:
You may know Florence Nightingale as a nurse
who helped sick people. But did you also know
that she was good at math? When she was young,
Nightingale liked playing with numbers. She enjoyed
counting travel time and distance on family trips.
Then she gathered the numbers and recorded them
as data. Nightingale knew that data was important.
She used data to solve problems.
During the Crimean War, Nightingale went to the
battlefield to help sick soldiers. The hospital was
much worse than she thought. It was dirty, messy,
and full of bugs! Nightingale knew that dirty
hospitals could be bad for the soldiers. More
soldiers got sick and died in the dirty hospital than
in battle. She wanted to change that. She asked
England to make the hospital much cleaner and
safer. However, the leaders of England didn’t
understand. To help them see the problem, she
collected data about the number of wounded and
dead soldiers. However, showing her findings with
just numbers was difficult.
To solve this problem, Nightingale created a
simple picture. It is called Nightingale’s rose
diagram. The diagram looked like a rose with
twelve petals. Each petal showed a month, and
larger petals meant more deaths. In the rose
diagram, three different colors were used by
Nightingale: blue, red, and black. Blue is for disease,
red is for battle wounds, and black is for other
causes. Surprisingly, (A)the blue part was the
largest! Nightingale used this diagram to show her
data simply and clearly. She was very smart and
creative.
When people saw Nightingale’s rose diagram, they
were amazed. It helped them understand that
(B)______________________________________________________.
Thanks to the rose diagram, hospitals became much
cleaner and safer. Nightingale’s love for data and
smart ideas saved many lives. She is still respected
by people around the world today.

body:
Many students have “turtle neck.” This happens
when their head sticks forward. It often comes from
using smartphones, studying, or sitting for a long
time. When you have turtle neck, you may get neck
pain, back pain, or headaches. But don’t worry!
Here are some easy stretches _______________________.
Desk Stretch
Sit up straight and move your head slowly from
side to side. Put your right hand on the left side of
your head. Then gently pull your head to the right.
Hold for 5 seconds. Repeat on your left side.
Finally, put your hands together and hold your chin
with your thumbs. Push your head back slowly.
Hold for 10 seconds. If you do this set of stretches,
you’ll feel better.

answer: push our head back with our thumb for 10 seconds

body:
Standing Stretch
Stand and spread your feet. Bend your arms to
make a W shape. Then lean your head backward.
Look up at a 45-degree angle. (A)Hold for 10
seconds. This stretch is great for your neck and
shoulders.
Bedtime Stretch
Lie on your bed with your head at the edge. Let
your head hang off the bed. Hold for 60 seconds.
Don’t do this for longer than 60 seconds. It can
make you feel dizzy. This stretch helps relax your
neck and back.
One thing is more important than stretching: good
habits in everyday life. Don’t look down at your
smartphone or computer monitor. Try to keep it at
eye level. When you are sitting, sit up straight and
keep your feet on the floor. If you are studying for
a long time, you should stretch every 50 minutes.
Good habits keep your neck healthy and strong.

Viral Marketing
Yuna: That’s the hottest dress on social media now.
Lots of people are wearing it. I have to get
that dress, too!

saw it again and again on social media. It isn't just
you. There are a lot of people (A)___________ fall for
a viral marketing strategy. Why?

quickly and widely on the Internet, just like a

social media, people naturally want to have it. Yuna,
just remember that a popular product isn't always
right for you.

따라서 답은 ①이다.

body:
Anchoring Effect
Somi: I'm ⓐ(look) for a lipstick for my mom.
Salesperson: How about this?
Somi: Expensive! I thought I could buy a lipstick for
30 dollars.
Salesperson: This is also popular.
Somi: That's better!
Hold on, Somi! Your budget is 30 dollars, but you
are buying a 40-dollar lipstick. The 40-dollar lipstick
sounds cheap only because the salesperson showed
you a 50-dollar lipstick first. This is an example of
the anchoring effect.
Usually, the first piece of information becomes an
“anchor” and ⓑ(influence) the shopper’s decision. In
your case, the 50-dollar lipstick was the anchor.
Somi, don’t just (A)______________ the first piece of
information that ⓒ(be) given to you.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에 주어진 단어의 알맞은 형태가 바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
solution:
1. ⓐ be동사 am 뒤의 진행형(be+-ing)이므로 I’m looking for ~ → looking.
2. ⓑ 주어 the first piece of information(단수)의 동사 becomes와 and로 나란히 연결되므로 influences.
3. ⓒ 관계대명사 that의 선행사 the first piece of information이 단수이므로 is.
따라서 답은 ②이다.

Yesterday, Jisu gave a birthday gift to her little
brother Jihoo. Later, she got the following text
message.
- I loved your gift. Thanks a lot. ·
 “Only one smiling face (·)? I ⓐguess he didn’t
like my gift,” Jisu thought.
When we talk with someone, we use not only
words but also facial ⓑexpressions and body
language. In texting, we use emojis instead.
Sometimes, a little emoji like ··can speak louder
than many words. The problem is that not
everybody uses emojis in the same way. Some
people like to use them a lot, and some don’t. In
addition, the same emojis can mean different things
to different people.
Sometimes, you need to pick up the phone.
Amy just got the following text message from her
best friend Nari.
- Did you really talk behind my back? I want you
to apologize to me.
Amy wanted to text Nari and ⓒexplain the
situation, but she thought again. “Well, this is too
much for a text,” she said to herself and called Nari.
Texting is okay for ⓓcasual situations, but
sometimes, you need to pick up the phone. This is
because ⓔmisunderstandings can easily happen
when you text. Do you need to talk about sensitive
issues with your friends? Then, don’t text them. Call
them instead.

<보기>
ⓐ to find the right answer to a question or the
truth based on all the facts
ⓑ something you say, write, or do that shows
what you think or feel
ⓒ to tell somebody about something in a way
that makes it easy to understand
ⓓ not formal or not for a formal situation
ⓔ a problem that is caused by not understanding
something correctly
solution: ⓒ 설명하다: 누군가에게 무언가를 이해하기 쉽게 만드는 방식 으로 말하다 ⓓ 일상적인: 공식적이 아니거나 공식적 상황을 위한 것이 아닌 ⓔ 오해: 무언가를 올바르게 이해하지 않음으로써 발생하는 문제

body:
다음 <보기>의 영영풀이가 알맞지 않은 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
ⓐ shopper: someone who sells something
ⓑ effect: a change that is caused by an event,
action etc.
ⓒ souvenir: a piece of paper with information about
your payment
ⓓ product: a thing that someone grows, produces,
or creates to sell
ⓔ budget: the amount of money you have to
pay for something
solution: ⓐ shopper는 ‘구매자’라는 뜻이며, 주어진 영영풀이인 ‘무언가 를 파는 사람’은 seller(파는 사람)의 풀이에 해당한다. 따라서 ‘someone who buys things in shops(가게에서 물건을 사는 사 람)’로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ souvenir는 ‘기념품’이라는 뜻이며 주어진 영영풀이인 ‘당신 의 지불에 대한 정보를 가진 종이 한 장’은 receipt(영수증)의 풀이에 해당한다. 따라서 ‘an object that you buy or keep to remind yourself of a special occasion or a place(특별한 행사 나 장소를 스스로에게 상기시키기 위해 당신이 사거나 보관하 는 물건)’로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ budget은 ‘예산’이라는 뜻이며, 주어진 영영풀이인 ‘무언가에 대해 당신이 지불해야만 하는 돈의 양’은 price(가격)의 풀이에 해 당한다. 따라서 ‘the amount of money that you have available to spend(당신이 소비할 수 있는 돈의 양)’으로 고쳐야 한다.

Do you think you are a smart shopper? Well, you
may think ⓐyou are, but hold on! There are
various marketing strategies ⓑwhich influence your
decisions. Learning about them will make you ⓒa
smarter shopper.
Hunger Marketing
Junho: What? The sale ends in two hours? If I don’t
buy the sneakers now, I will have to buy
them at a higher price.
Stop, Junho! You’re buying the sneakers just
because you don’t want to miss the sale. You’re
falling for a hunger marketing strategy.
ⓓIf people can buy a product only for a limited
time, they often feel “hungry” for it and want to
buy it. About missing the sale, ⓔdon’t worry,
Junho. You’ll soon see a similar sale again.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(C)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?

(A) By learning about marketing strategies, we can
become better shoppers. (T/F)
(B) Junho tries to buy the sneakers because there
is a limited number of them. (T/F)
(C) Through hunger marketing, people feel that they
may purchase a product at any time. (T/F)
solution: 차례대로 T-F-F이다. (A) 마케팅 전략들을 배움으로써, 우리는 더 나은 구매자가 될 수 있다. (T) (일치) (B) 준호는 그 운동화의 한정된 개수가(→세일 시간이) 있기 때 문에 그것을 사려고 한다. (F) (불일치) (C) 헝거 마케팅을 통해, 사람들은 언제든지(→제한된 시간에 만) 그 제품을 구매할 수 있을 것이라고 느낀다. (F) (불일치)

Hunger Marketing
Junho: What? The sale ends in two hours? If I don’t
buy the sneakers now, I will have to buy
them at a (A)[lower / higher] price.
Stop, Junho! You’re buying the sneakers just
because you don’t want to miss the sale. You’re
falling for a hunger marketing strategy.
If people can buy a product only for a limited
time, they often feel “hungry” for it and want to
buy it. About missing the sale, don’t worry, Junho.
You’ll soon see a similar sale again.
Viral Marketing
Yuna: That’s the hottest dress on social media now.
Lots of people are wearing it. I have to get
that dress, too!
Wait, Yuna! You only want the dress because you
saw it again and again on social media. It isn't just
you. There are a lot of people who fall for a viral
marketing strategy. Why?
Information about a product can spread (B)[quickly
/ slowly] and widely on the Internet, just like a
“virus.” If a product becomes hot on social media,
people naturally want to have it. Yuna, just
remember that a popular product isn't always right
for you.
Anchoring Effect
Somi: I'm looking for a lipstick for my mom.
Salesperson: How about this?
Somi: Expensive! I thought I could buy a lipstick for
30 dollars.
Salesperson: This is also popular.
Somi: That's better!
Hold on, Somi! Your budget is 30 dollars, but you
are buying a 40-dollar lipstick. The 40-dollar lipstick
sounds cheap only because the salesperson showed
you a 50-dollar lipstick first. This is an example of
the anchoring effect.
Usually, the first piece of information becomes an
“anchor” and influences the shopper’s decision. In
your case, the (C)[40-dollar / 50-dollar] lipstick was
the anchor. Somi, don’t just rely on the first piece
of information that is given to you.

solution: (A) 완전한 절 ‘The first webcam was invented’에 이어 흐름상 ‘지켜보기 위해’라는 뜻을 나타내야 하므로, 앞의 to와 함께 ‘목 적’을 나타내는 부사적용법의 to부정사(to+동사원형)를 이루는 동사원형 watch가 적절하다. (B) ‘~이 있다’라는 뜻의 ‘there+be동사+주어(명사구)’ 구문으 로, 주어가 단수명사구 only one coffee machine이므로 주어에 수일치한 단수형 과거 be동사 was가 적절하다. (C) ‘~해야 한다’라는 뜻의 ‘have/has+to부정사’ 구문의 과거형 은 ‘had+to부정사‘로 쓰므로 had 뒤의 to와 함께 to부정사(to+ 동사원형)를 이루는 동사원형 make가 적절하다.

made traveling difficult. Why? In those days, people

riders simply pushed the bicycle forward with their
feet. The present-day bicycle is the result of many

You can work with NGOs as a teenager. It is a
great way to learn about social issues and make
the world better. Are you interested? Then, read
Inho’s blog below.
JAN 5
I grew up in Jeju-do, so I had many chances to
see dolphins. Then, I learned that many dolphins
are in danger. Some are even endangered. I
thought I should do something. So, I searched the
Internet and found an NGO, Dolphin Lovers. It does
various activities such as cleaning up beaches and
helping dolphins. After some thought, I joined it
today.
JAN 20
Many dolphins get sick or even die because of
plastic waste and fishing nets, so cleaning up
beaches is important. There was a beach cleanup
party today, and I took part in it. Cleaning up the
beach was not easy, but I enjoyed it. Oh, I saw
Aunt Sumi there. She is also a member of Dolphin
Lovers. What a small world!

need to learn some skills. They will need them to
survive in the wild. I really wanted to be part of
the project. Luckily, I got the chance. I just ran
some errands in the training class today, but the
experience made me so excited.
APR 22
Today, Halla and Olle went back to the sea. There
was a small ceremony, and all the members of
Dolphin Lovers were there. The ceremony made us
quite emotional. In fact, I cried a little. Now I
cannot see Halla and Olle anymore! However, I was
very happy at the same time. After 10 years of
hard life in an aquarium, now all the sea is their
home. “Live freely and happily ever after!” I shouted
and waved goodbye to them.

when they sit in a tree, they look just like part of
the tree. They become almost (A)[invisible /
invisibly] to other animals. This gives them a huge
advantage in the wild!

almost all the way around. They can scan their

(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 문장의 동사 become의 보어 자리이며 보어 자리에는 부사 가 아닌 형용사가 쓰이므로 부사 almost의 수식을 받아 형용 사구를 이루도록 형용사 invisible이 적절하다. (B) 전치사 by의 목적어 자리이므로 명사(구) 또는 동명사(구) 모두 올 수 있으나 뒤에 목적어인 their heads가 이어지므로 목적어를 취할 수 있는 동명사  moving이 적절하다. my friend Amelia at the airport, I was so excited. I
ⓐhave known her since I was 10 years old. She

Beautiful Palace
We got on the famous red bus and the first stop
was Buckingham Palace. The King and his family
live there. We saw the King's Guard. The guards
were wearing red jackets and tall black hats. We
took pictures near them, but they didn't smile or
move. They were like statues!
Yummy Meal
Next, we went to Camden Market. This market is
known for its food from around the world. Amelia
told me to try the fish and chips. I thought, "How
strange! I ⓑhave eaten fish many times. But I've
never tried it with potato chips." But when the food
came out, I found out that they call French fries
"chips" in London! After a yummy British meal, we
walked around the market. We saw the famous red
phone booth and took more pictures. Then I bought
a pretty plate for my mom. ⓒWhat a fun day!
Magical Experience
London often has rainy weather. It rained a little
today, but Amelia didn’t have an umbrella. She said
that most Londoners use umbrellas only for heavy
rain. I was surprised ⓓto hear that. I asked Amelia
to take me to King’s Cross Station. I wanted to see
this train station because of the Harry Potter
movies. They were filmed at this station. Look! We

were in the movies. We took lots of selfies. Can
you find the secret way to Hogwarts?
Traveling Underground
It was time to go home. Amelia said, “Let’s take the
tube.” I asked, “What’s the tube?” She told me, “In
London, we ⓔcall the subway the tube. That’s
because the subway tunnels are round like a tube.”
On the tube, Amelia asked me, “Red is a special color
in London. Did you see many red things?” I certainly
did! How many red things can you spot in my photos?

solution: 두 번째 문장의 주어인 It이 첫 번째 문장의 the new shop을 가리키고 있으므로 두 문장을 서로 이어주는 접속사와 주어 역 할의 대명사라는 두 가지 역할을 동시에 하는 주격 관계대명사 를 이용하여 연결한 형태인 I like the new shop+관계사절(주 격 관계대명사+동사 ~)의 형태가 되어야 한다. 선행사인 the new shop은 사물이므로 관계대명사 that 또는 which가 와야 하고, 주격 관계대명사 뒤에 이어지는 동사는 선행사에 수일치 해야 하므로 단수명사구인 선행사 the new shop에 수일치한 단수동사 sells가 쓰여야 한다. 따라서 두 문장을 연결한 것으로 ❷ ‘I like the new shop that sells strange things.(나는 이상한 물건들을 파는 그 새로운 가게를 좋아해.)‘가 적절하다.

There once was a lovely family with three children.
The children were very close. But ⓐas they got
older, they slowly grew apart. One day, the parents
called the children together. “Do you remember this
room? You used to play here. It was always filled
with happiness,” said the father. The mother continued,
“But now, you don’t even talk to each other. So,
we made a puzzle for you. Here are three silver
coins. Go to the market and buy something ⓑto fill
this room completely. If you succeed, you will get a
big reward.”
Ethan, the eldest child, said, “We will do our best.”
The youngest of the family, Annie, was puzzled.
“Three silver coins aren’t enough to fill this room!”
The father replied, “If you work together, you can
figure it out. ⓒThree heads are better than one.”
Patrick, the middle child, shouted, “I know the
answer!” He grabbed a silver coin and ran out the
door.
Patrick returned after he bought two bags of
feathers from the market. He began to fill the room
with feathers, but they barely covered the floor.
Ethan said to Patrick, “Why did you act on your
own?” Patrick dropped his head. “I’m sorry. I ⓓ
thought I knew the answer.” Annie sighed. “Now we
only have two coins ⓔleft.”
The children went to the market together. Patrick
had another idea. “How about straw? It’s cheaper
than feathers, but it takes up more space.” Ethan
said, “Great idea! But let’s only use one coin for
now.” “Good thinking! That way, we can play it
safe,” said Annie. Ethan continued, “If straw is not
the answer, we will have one more chance with the
last coin.”
They returned home with six bundles of straw. The
straw came up to their knees, but it wasn’t enough.
Ethan said, “We need to think differently. How
about water?” Patrick said, “The water would just
leak out of the room. Perhaps the answer isn’t
something physical after all.” Annie yelled, “That’s it!
I know the answer. Let’s go to the market again.”
When they got back home, Annie took a candle
out of her bag. The candle was lit by Patrick, and
the entire room was filled with light. The mother
yelled excitedly, “You solved the puzzle!” Now, they
could see drawings on the wall. “Look! That’s us!
Our family,” said Annie. Patrick said, “I remember
these drawings. They were drawn by us when we
were little.” Ethan turned to his parents. “Now I
understand. The greatest reward in the world is my
family.”

body:
It is easy to experience popcorn brain when you
do many things at the same time on your
smartphone. You keep moving down the screen and
clicking, and many thoughts pop up quickly, like
popcorn in a pan! If it happens at night, you may
have trouble sleeping.
More importantly, people with popcorn brain have
trouble paying attention. They cannot concentrate
on one thing for a long time. In a study, people
were able to focus on one thing for 2.5 minutes in
2004. Nowadays, people can only concentrate for
47 seconds. If you do not want to have popcorn
brain, you need to make some changes. Here are
some tips.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(C)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?

(A) Doing many things at once on your smartphone
causes you to experience "popcorn brain"
more. (T/F)
(B) Those who have popcorn brain aren’t able to
pay attention to one thing for a long time.
(T/F)
(C) People's focus time is over two minutes
shorter than in 2004. (T/F)
solution: 차례대로 T-T-F이다. (A) 스마트폰으로 한 번에 많은 일을 하는 것은 여러분이 팝콘 브레인을 더 경험하게 한다. (T) (일치) (B) 팝콘 브레인을 갖고 있는 사람들은 오랜 시간 동안 한 가 지 일에 집중을 못한다. (T) (일치) (C) 사람들의 집중 시간은 2004년보다 2분 이상(→1분 43초) 더 짧다. (F) (불일치)

body:
Imagine this — you are doing your homework at
your desk. Suddenly, you remember that your mom
asked you to call her. When you (A)pick up your
smartphone, a message pops up. It is for a new
video from your favorite channel. You watch the
video and (B)keep watching many other short
videos. Then, you hear another sound. There is a
(C)sale on the shoes that you really want. You were
going to ask your mom to buy them for you. Wait,
you forgot to call her two hours ago! If this story
feels like yours, you may have “popcorn brain.”
It is easy to experience popcorn brain when you
do many things at the same time on your
smartphone. You keep moving down the screen and
clicking, and many thoughts pop up quickly, like
popcorn in a pan! If it happens at night, you may
have trouble sleeping.
More importantly, people with popcorn brain have
trouble paying attention. They cannot concentrate
on one thing for a long time. In a study, people
were able to focus on one thing for 2.5 minutes in
2004. Nowadays, people can only concentrate for
47 seconds. If you do not want to have popcorn
brain, you need to make some changes. Here are
some (D)tips.
Tips
Put away your phone.
(E)Leave it in another room when you need to
focus.
Get moving.
Play some sports with your friends.
Enjoy the small things in life.
Feel the sunshine and look at the sky.
Try to focus on one thing for a long time.
Read a book.
Smartphones are useful. They connect people and
make life easier. However, using them too much
can hurt your brain and your mind. It is important
to cut down on screen time. Are you ready to give
it a try?

Sugar on Snow
Hi, I’m Olivia. I live in Quebec, Canada. Every
spring, we hold maple syrup festivals. People get
sap from maple trees and boil it (A)to make maple
syrup. During the festivals, we enjoy pancakes with
the syrup. Some people even drink it by itself! We
enjoy maple candy, too. People also call it “sugar
on snow.” To make it, just pour hot syrup onto
snow and wrap it around a stick. It’s sweet and
soft!

Sugar on Snow
Hi, I’m Olivia. I live in Quebec, Canada. Every
spring, we hold maple syrup festivals.
People get sap from maple trees and boil it to
make maple syrup. During the festivals, we enjoy
pancakes with the syrup. Some people even drink it
by itself! We enjoy maple candy, too. People also
call it “sugar on snow.” To make it,
just pour hot syrup onto snow and wrap it around
a stick. It’s sweet and soft!

Canadians are not willing to drink maple syrup by itself.
Maple candy has another name, “sugar on snow.”

some tips.

Hi, I’m Mateo from Mexico City. In Mexico, we
celebrate a holiday, Día de Muertos. It means “Day
of the Dead.” In November, we gather together to
remember family members who passed away. We
visit their graves with their photos, flowers, and
traditional foods as gifts. We also share sugar skulls
and pan de muerto with our family and friends.
Pan de muerto is a traditional kind of bread for the
dead. We usually use sugar skulls as decorations.
This year, I made some sugar skulls with my
friends. Look! Do you like them?

Hi, I’m Mateo from Mexico City. In Mexico, we
celebrate a holiday, Día de Muertos. It means “Day
of the Dead.” In November, we gather together to
remember family members who passed away. We
visit their graves with their photos, flowers, and
traditional foods as gifts. We also share sugar skulls
and pan de muerto with our family and friends.

dead. We usually use sugar skulls as decorations.
This year, I made some sugar skulls with my
friends. Look! Do you like them?

body:
다음 글을 읽고 아래 질문에 대한 대답을 완성할 때, 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

Hazel: I have this cute pouch in my bag. It’s my snack pouch. I put candies, jellies, and snack bars in it. I like to try out the newest snacks. These are ramyeon jellies. They look like ramyeon but taste sweet. My friends are also interested in my snacks. So, I bring extra snacks for them. I share chocolate bars with Kate for some energy before P.E. class. Are you worried about my teeth? Don’t worry. I don’t forget to brush them. I always have a toothbrush in my bag.

Q. What does Hazel do before P.E. class?
→ She ⓐ_____________ chocolate bars with Kate to ⓑ_____________ energy.
solution:
1. 본문에서 Hazel은 체육 수업 전에 힘을 얻으려고(for some energy) Kate와 초콜릿 바를 나눠 먹는다고 했다.
2. ⓐ에는 ‘먹다’의 뜻인 has(have chocolate bars = 초콜릿 바를 먹다)가, ⓑ에는 ‘얻다’의 뜻인 gain이 알맞다.
3. use up(다 써 버리다)은 흐름과 반대이고, makes·breaks는 초콜릿 바를 나눠 먹는다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
4. 따라서 답은 ④이다.

ⓑ What is it for?
ⓒ What is it like?
ⓓ How do you use it?
ⓔ What is this used for?
ⓕ What do people use it for?
solution: 남자는 빈칸의 질문과 함께 그것이 등산용이라는 질문하고 있 으며 여자는 그것(=막대기)이 등산용이 아니라, 시각 장애인들 을 돕기 위한 것이라며 그 용도를 답하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 물건의 용도를 묻는 표현이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 ⓑ '그건 무엇을 위한거니?‘, ⓓ ’그것을 어떻게 사용하니?‘, ⓔ ’이것은 무엇에 사용되니?, ⓕ‘사람들은 그것을 무엇에 사용하니?’가 알 맞다.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 문장의 동사 자리로, 주어 자리에 ‘All+관계사절‘이 쓰였으 며, 이때 all이 상황을 가리킬 때는 단수 취급한다. 따라서 All 이 목적격 관계대명사 that이 생략된 관계사절(I can do)의 수 식을 받아서 흐름상 ‘내가 할 수 있는 모든 것, 유일한 것’이라 는 상황을 의미하므로, 단수동사 is가 적절하다. (B) 뒤에 문장의 동사 is가 있으므로, 앞의 명사 My dream을 수식하여 주어부를 이루는 준동사 자리가 되어야 한다. 따라서 형용사적 용법의 to부정사인 to go가 적절하다. (C) ‘…가 ~하도록 만들다[시키다]’의 의미를 갖는 ‘사역동사 make+목적어+목적격보어‘의 구조로, 사역동사 make는 목적격 보어로 동사원형을 취하므로 make의 목적어 my men에 이어 진 목적격보어로 동사원형 return이 알맞다.

body:
Everyone (A)[has / have] a job in my class. The
most popular one is to feed our class pet, Larry,
the iguana. This week, I have to take care of him.
It is Friday and I am walking back home. I see a
woman who is walking with her pet dog.
Huh? Pet? Larry?
I turn around and run back to the classroom.
The cage is open, and Larry is gone.
Oh, no! Where is Larry? What should I tell my
classmates?
My mind turns into a worry machine. I begin to
breathe quickly.
Think, Oliver, think! What should I do? I have
friends (B)[who / which] can help me.
I call and ask them (C)[coming / to come] right away.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) Everyone은 ‘모두’라는 뜻이지만 주어 자리에 쓰이면 항상 단수 취급하므로, 단수동사 has가 알맞다. (B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can help me)을 이끌어, 앞의 사 람을 가리키는 선행사 friends를 수식해야 하므로 주격 관계대 명사 who가 알맞다. (C) ‘ask+목적어+목적격보어(…에게 ~할 것을 요청[부탁]하다) ‘의 의미를 갖는 5형식 동사 ask는 to부정사를 목적격보어로 취하므로, 목적어 them 뒤의 목적격 자리에 to부정사 to come이 알맞다.

solution: (A) 남극 대륙을 향해 떠났지만, 근처 해안에서 배가 두꺼운 얼음에 부딪혔고, 이후 겨울이 지날 때까지 기다려야만 한다는 내용이 이어지므로, 배가 ‘갇혔다(stuck)'는 흐름이 자연스럽다. August 1914.

ⓑmelting. But, the ice broke the ship into pieces.

solution: (A) ‘~이/가 있다’라는 뜻의 ‘There+be동사+주어 ~’ 구문으로, 주어의 핵심이 단수명사구 one story이므로 이에 수일치한 단 수 be동사 is가 적절하다. (B) 시간 접속사 When이 쓰인 부사절(When the English army ~ century)에 이어진 주절의 동사 자리로, 부사절의 시제가 과 거(was)이므로 주절의 동사도 이에 시제를 일치한 과거가 되도 록 과거형 동사 came이 적절하다. (C) 주어 People에 이어진 동사 parade, dance와 등위접속사 and 로 ‘A, B, and C’의 구조를 이루어야 하므로 동사 sing이 적절하다.

solution: (A) 과거의 일임을 나타내는 부사절(when the bell rang)이 쓰여 종이 울 렸을 때 무엇을 하고 있었는지 나타내야 하며, 앞에 be동사 was가 쓰 였으므로 과거의 진행 중인 동작을 나타내는 과거진행형(be동사 과거 형+현재분사(동사원형+-ing))을 이루는 현재분사 talking이 적절하다. (B) 조건 접속사 if가 쓰인 절의 동사 자리로, 주절에 미래 조동사 will이 쓰여 미래의 일을 나타내더라도 조건 부사절에서는 현재시제가 미래의 일을 나타내므로 주어 we에 수일치한 현재형 be동사 are가 적절하다. (C) 흐름상 응급처지 방법을 설명하는 글이므로 ‘~하라’ 또는 ‘~하지 말라’라는 뜻의 명령문이 되어야 하며 부정 명령문은 ‘Don’t[Do not]+ 동사원형‘으로 쓰므로 Do not 뒤에 동사원형 move가 적절하다.

solution: (A) 문장 앞에 장소 부사 There(거기에)가 오면 뒤에 주어와 동 사의 순서가 바뀌어 ‘동사+주어’가 되지만 주어가 대명사인 경 우에는 ‘주어+동사’ 순으로 쓴다. 따라서 문장 맨 앞의 부사 There 뒤에 주어가 대명사 he이므로 ‘주어+동사’의 어순인 he is가 적절하다. (B) 뒤의 형용사 happy와 결과를 나타내는 that절(that she ~ him)과 함께 ‘너무 ~해서 …하다’라는 뜻의 원인과 결과를 나타 내는 ’so+형용사+that+주어+동사 ~’의 구문을 이루어야 하므 로 형용사 happy 앞에 부사로 so가 적절하다. (C) 주어 Robbie에 이어진 과거형 동사 saw와 뒤의 과거형 동 사 saved와 등위접속사 and로 ‘A, B, and C’의 구조로 병렬 연 결되어야 하므로 같은 형태의 과거형 동사 ran이 적절하다.

saying is literally true. Dogs have been an important
part of Nepalese culture for hundreds of years. The
Nepalese believe that dogs are helpers of the god

put a red mark on dogs’ foreheads to wish them
good luck. They even bow to dogs to show them
love and thanks.

다음 우리말을 바르게 영작한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

그녀는 너무 어려서 운전을 할 수 없었다.
ⓐ She was so young to drive a car.
ⓑ She was too young to drive a car.
ⓒ She was so young that she can‘t drive a car.
ⓓ She was so young that she couldn’t drive a car.
ⓔ She was too young that she couldn’t drive a car.
solution: ‘매우[너무] ~해서 ….할 수 없다’라는 뜻은 ‘so+형용사/부사+that+주 어+can’t+동사원형 ~‘으로 쓰며, ’too+형용사/부사+to부정사 ~’ 로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다. 주어진 문장은 be동사 was가 쓰였으므로 was의 보어로 부사가 아닌 형용사(young)가 쓰여야 하며, ‘so ~ that’ 구문의 경우 주절의 과거 was에 시제 일치하여 that이 이 끄는 결과의 문장에 can’t가 아닌 과거형 couldn’t를 써야 한다.

through body movements, and it has passed down
stories from one generation to the next.

with later generations. (T/F)

Now it’s time to dance! Remember that you
become a storyteller when you dance hula. You tell
a story with your hands, feet, and hips. Oh, you
need to (A)[remove / wear] your shoes and socks!
Hula is always done barefoot.
Let’s start with the hand gestures. Every gesture in
hula has a meaning. Wave your fingers while you
move your arms up and down. This gesture is
called ua in the Hawaiian language, and it means
“rain.” What about the sun? Hawaiians make a circle
with their arms above their heads. That’s ka lā, the
“sun.” These gestures are so (B)[complicated /
simple] that you can easily remember them.
Next, bend your knees a little and step from side
to side. While you step to the side, move your hips
naturally. Now move your hands with your hips and
feet!
Well, time’s up! That’s all for today. Remember
that hula is not just a dance. Hula is a language
and a way of storytelling, so it is (C)[unimportant /
important] to Hawaiians. As a hula teacher, I always
try to continue the history and culture of Hawaii. If
you want to learn more, come to my next class.
Everyone is welcome. Aloha!
(A)
(B)
(C)

In 1903, a French scientist, Mr. Bénédictus, was
(A)[experimenting / experimented] with liquid plastic
in a glass flask. He accidentally hit the glass flask,
and it fell on the floor. “Oops!” Although the glass
flask was broken into pieces, they still held together
in the shape of the flask! How could this happen?
The secret was the liquid plastic in the flask. This
finding led to his invention of safety glass. These
days, we can find safety glass everywhere. For
example, it (B)[is used / uses] for car windows. If
there (C)[are / is] a car accident, people are safer
from sharp pieces of glass.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(C)
solution: (A) Mr. Bénédictus와 동격을 이루고 있는 주어인 a French scientist가 ‘실험을 하는’ 주체이며, ‘실험하다’라는 뜻의 동사 experiment는 목적어 없이 쓰는 자동사로, 자동사는 수동태로 쓰지 않으므로 과거형 be동사 was와 함께 과거진행형(was/ were+현재분사(동사원형+-ing))을 이루는 현재분사 experimenting 이 적절하다. (B) 주어 it(=safety glass)은 자동차 창문을 위해 ‘사용되는’ 대 상이므로 주어 it에 맞는 be동사 is를 사용한 수동태(be동사+ 과거분사)인 is used가 적절하다. (C) ‘~이 있다’라는 뜻의 ‘there+be동사+주어’ 구문으로, 주어가 단수명사구인 a car accident이므로 단수동사 is가 적절하다.

Time passed. One day, Bobby’s dad looked very
sad. He told Bobby, “Bob fell ill. He is in a hospital
which is far from here.”
(A) Suddenly, Bob made a small sound like sneezing.
At that moment, Bobby realized that Bob would
recover soon. And Bob did. Slowly, Bob began
to talk a little and move his fingers. But he still
couldn’t walk.
(B) Bob came back home after a few months. He just
lay in bed without talking or moving. After a while,
Bobby came into Bob’s room with the blocks.
“Bob, it’s time to build a tower!”
Bob’s mouth made a small smile. Bobby began
to build the tower.
“Okay, Bob, now the elephant block.”
(C) “I want to see him,” Bobby said.
“You can’t, Bobby,” Mom told him. “He can’t move
his arms and legs, and he can’t talk. We’ll just
have to wait and hope that he will get better.”
solution: Bobby가 아빠에게서 할아버지 Bob이 편찮으셔서 멀리 있는 병원에 계신다는 소식을 들은 주어진 글에 이어, 할아버지를 보고 싶은 Bobby에게 엄마가 Bob의 증상을 얘기해주며 그저 회복되기를 기다려야 한다고 말한 (C), 몇 달 후 Bob이 집으로 돌아왔으나 침대에 누워만 있는 그의 방에 Bobby가 블록을 가지고 들어가 탑을 쌓기 시작하는 (B), Bob이 재채기 같은 작 은 소리를 내자 Bobby는 Bob이 곧 회복될 것임을 깨달았고 천천히 회복되었다는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. 천재(소영순) 2과

Bobby got his name from his grandfather, Bob. Bob
was his best friend. Bob was the person ⓐwhat
taught Bobby how to walk.
“Hold my hands, Bobby,” Bob said.
“Now one foot, now ⓑother.”
Bob and Bobby often played with old wooden
blocks. They slowly piled the blocks one by one
ⓒto build a tower.
“There ⓓare one more block (A)to build,” Bob said.
“And that’s the elephant block,” Bobby said.
Bobby carefully put the elephant block on the top.
But Bob sneezed, and the tower fell. Bobby laughed
and laughed. Bobby said, “You ⓔalways sneeze
when the elephant block appears.”

위 대화를 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: How did Bobby get his name?
What did Bob and Bobby often play with?
How many blocks were there before the elephantblock?
What did Bobby do when the tower fell?
solution: Bobby가 꼭대기에 마지막 코끼리 블록을 올려놓는 것은 언급 되었으나, 그 전에 얼마나 많은 블록을 쌓았는지는 알 수 없으 므로 ❹ ‘코끼리 블록 전에 얼마나 많은 블록들이 있었는가?’는 답할 수 없는 질문이다.

body:
Time passed. One day, Bobby’s dad looked very
ⓐsad. He told Bobby, “Bob fell ill. He is in a
hospital which is far from here.”
“I want to see him,” Bobby said.
“You can’t, Bobby,” Mom told him. “He can’t move
his arms and legs, and he can’t talk. We’ll just have
to wait and hope ⓑthat he will get better.”
Bob came back home after a few ⓒmonths. He
just lay in bed without talking or ⓓmoving. After a
while, Bobby came into Bob’s room with the blocks.
“Bob, it’s time ⓔto building a tower!”
Bob’s mouth made a small smile. Bobby began to
build the tower.
“Okay, Bob, now the elephant block.”
Suddenly, Bob made a small sound like sneezing. At
that moment, Bobby realized that Bob would recover
soon. And Bob did. Slowly, Bob began to talk a little
and move his fingers. But he still couldn’t walk.

윗글에 드러난 Bobby의 심경 변화로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 할아버지가 아파서 멀리 있는 병원에 계신다는 소식을 듣고 할 아버지를 보고 싶어 했으며, 몇 달 후 집으로 돌아오셨으나 침 대에 누워만 있는 Bob을 위해 블록을 가지고 할아버지 방으로 가는 것으로 보아, Bob이 할아버지를 걱정하고 있음을 알 수 있으며, Bob이 재채기 같은 작은 소리를 내자 Bob이 곧 회복 하실 것이라는 것을 Bobby가 깨달았고, 천천히 회복되었다는 내용에서 Bobby가 희망적인 마음을 느꼈음을 알 수 있다. 따라 서 ❹ ‘걱정하는 → 희망적인’이 Bobby의 심경으로 알맞다.

(C) 시간의 부사절(When I was little)에 이어지는 주절의 주어 you 의 동사인 과거동사 held와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬구조를 이루어야 하며, 과거에 있었던 일이므로 과거동사 said가 적절하다.

Aloha! Welcome to Hawaii! Aloha means “hello” or
“goodbye” in the Hawaiian language. I’m Malia, and
I’m your hula teacher for today. Have you heard of
hula before? How much do you know about hula?
Before we start our lesson, I want to tell you about it.
Hula is a traditional dance from Hawaii, and it
(A)has been a part of Hawaiian life for a long time.
The early Hawaiians didn’t have a writing system, so
they used hula to tell stories. Hula is a language
through body movements, and it has passed down
stories from one generation to the next.
Now it’s time to dance! Remember that you
become a storyteller when you dance hula. You tell
a story with your hands, feet, and hips. Oh, you
need to take off your shoes and socks! Hula is
always done barefoot.
Let’s start with the hand gestures. Every gesture in
hula (B)________________. Wave your fingers while you
move your arms up and down. This gesture is
called ua in the Hawaiian language, and it means
“rain.” What about the sun? Hawaiians make a circle
with their arms above their heads. That’s ka lā, the
“sun.” (C)이 손동작들은 매우 단순해서 당신은 그것들
을 쉽게 기억할 수 있어요.
Next, bend your knees a little and step from side to
side. While you step to the side, move your hips naturally.
Now move your hands with your hips and feet!
Well, time’s up! That’s all for today. Remember
that hula is not just a dance. Hula is a language
and a way of storytelling, so it is important to
Hawaiians. As a hula teacher, I always try to
continue the history and culture of Hawaii. If you
want to learn more, come to my next class.
Everyone is welcome. Aloha!

다음 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?

W: Hello, Eric. How are you doing?
B: I’m doing okay, thanks. How’s your trip to London,
Grandma?
W: It’s great. I went to Big Ben and had a meat
pie yesterday.
B: Wow! You’re having a great time there. By the
way, what time is it in London now?
W: ____________________________________________
B: Oh, you woke up early! I hope you have a
wonderful vacation there.
ⓐ It’s midnight.
ⓑ It’s six fifteen a.m.
ⓒ Seven forty-five p.m.
ⓓ It’s a quarter to eight in the evening.
ⓔ It’s a quarter past six in the morning.
solution:
1. Eric이 런던은 지금 몇 시인지 묻고, 할머니의 대답을 들은 뒤 '일찍 일어나셨네요!'라고 말한다.
2. 따라서 이른 아침 시각이 알맞다. ⓑ It’s six fifteen a.m.과 ⓔ It’s a quarter past six in the morning.은 둘 다 오전 6시 15분이다.
3. ⓐ 자정, ⓒ·ⓓ 오후 7시 45분은 '일찍 일어났다'는 말과 맞지 않다.
따라서 답은 ②이다.

solution: 대화문의 밑줄 친 (A)의 ‘is it okay if ~?’는 ‘내가 ~해도 될까 요?’라는 뜻으로 어떤 일을 하기 전에 상대방에게 허락을 요청할 쓰는 표현이다. 따라서 ⓒ ‘is it alright if ~?’, ⓔ ‘could I ~?’ 의 표현으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다. 참고로, ⓑ의 ‘do you mind if ~?’도 허락을 요청하는 표현이지만 그 뜻이 ‘내가 ~하면 꺼리 세요?’라는 뜻이므로 상대방에게 괜찮다고 수락하기 위해서는 ‘Of course.’가 아니라 ‘Of course not.’으로 답해야 한다.

chocolate cookies. However, she didn’t have enough

(2) _________: ______________________

2. (E) 현재완료는 have[has]+과거분사이다. eat의 과거분사는 eaten이므로 ate → eaten.
3. (B) so hard that, (C) haven’t been to, (D) have just finished는 모두 바르다.
따라서 답은 (A) can’t → couldn’t, (E) ate → eaten이다.

Black and White Soccer Balls
Soccer balls today come in various colors, but
black and white balls are quite common. Have you
heard about the origin of this popular design?
Black and white balls came out ⓐduring the 1970
World Cup in Mexico. People could spot them
easily on their black and white TVs. Isn’t that
smart? Now we have color televisions, but we still
kick the classic black and white soccer balls.
The Uniform Colors
Players on each team wear uniforms with their
own colors. Uniform colors have the power to
(A)[break up / unite] the team under the same
spirit. They are also useful on the field. Players can
spot each other and make (B)[quick / hesitant]
decisions thanks to their team’s unique colors. On
the field, referees wear uniforms with (C)[normal /
special] colors because they need to stand out from
the players. Among several colors, black has been
their favorite. Black looks ⓑpowerful, and it sends a
strong “Don’t argue with me!” message.
Color Cards for Communication
Referees ⓒhave used yellow and red cards since
1970. Different color cards ⓓsend different
messages to players. Yellow cards say, “Be careful
with those fouls!” Red cards mean “You’re out!” All
players from different countries clearly understand
the meaning of these cards.
Do you have a plan ⓔto watch a soccer match?
Then check out the various colors on the field. It
will be more fun!

solution: (A) 등위 접속사 and로 완전한 절(you will forget about your worries)과 병렬 연결되어 있으므로 and 앞도 완전한 절이 되 어야 한다. 뒤에 명사구 the pieces가 이어져 절의 다른 동사 가 없고, 앞에도 다른 주어가 없으므로 완전한 절이 되기 위해 선 주어를 생략한 명령문이어야 한다. 명령문은 동사원형으로 시작하므로 동사원형 put이 적절하다. (B) 문장의 동사인 be동사 is에 대한 주어를 이루어야 하며, 주 어 자리에는 동사원형이 올 수 없고 동명사(구) 또는 to부정사 (구) 형태가 올 수 있으므로, 동명사 Doing이 적절하다. (C) 접속사 When이 이루는 부사절의 동사 자리로, 주절에 미 래 조동사 will이 쓰였으나 부사절에서는 현재시제가 미래를 나타내므로 ‘will+동사원형’ 형태는 쓸 수 없다. 따라서 복수주 어 you에 수일치한 복수동사 put이 적절하다.

body:
Kia Orana! I’m Nikau from New Zealand. I’m
working at a whale research center in the Cook
Islands. I think humpback whales are the most
amazing animals in the ocean. I have kept a diary
about them ⓐto record my work and thoughts.
July 1st
Finally, the humpback whales are back! They have
traveled about 6,500 km from the Southern Ocean
to give birth. The big and friendly giants came
close to our boat and played for a while. All of a
sudden, they jumped up high and made huge
splashes. Watching whales never ⓑgets boring.
July 17th
Today, I flew a drone to tag humpback whales. I
followed them closely and dropped tags carefully
onto their backs. We get a lot of information about
them from the tags. I am particularly interested in
their songs, and the tags ⓒhave recorded them for
several years. Their songs last up to 30 minutes
and can travel thousands of kilometers underwater!
The songs are beautiful, but we still don’t know
much about them.
August 2nd
I was filming some humpback whales underwater.
Suddenly, one whale came close and pushed me
hard. I tried to swim away, but it kept pushing me
out of the water. I was so surprised. Then
somebody shouted from the boat, “A tiger shark is
coming!” I safely got on the boat. I realized ⓓthat
the whale was trying to save me. Humpback whales
sometimes help other sea animals, but I never
expected them to save my life.
August 5th
This morning, I found a dead humpback whale on
the coast. There were so many plastic bags and
fishing nets in its stomach. Human activities are the
greatest danger to whales. The ocean is home to
whales and other sea animals. I want humans and
sea animals ⓔto live in harmony.
